articles.summary: The Trump administration is working with Venezuela to set up a path toward elections, according to a senior State Department official. The blueprint would see a new Supreme Court, or TSJ, put into place by mid-December of this year, followed shortly by a reformed, non-political National Electoral Council. According to the Trump administration, that would ultimately see the country’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, declare a vacancy in the presidency, triggering a six-month period for new elections. While the specific timeline remains unclear, the administration is pushing for it to happen while Trump is still in office. Trust “is going to be based on actions,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters when asked about the administration’s view of Rodríguez. articles.summary: The black vehicles with tinted windows converged on the bus stop just after 5:30 a.m. It was June 18, 2025, and Pedro Vasquez Perdomo and his co-workers were drinking coffee, waiting for a ride to a construction job in Pasadena, California. Masked, armed men poured from the vehicles and charged at them. Vasquez Perdomo thought they were probably immigration agents, but he couldn’t be sure. The agents wore plain clothes with no visible badges and didn’t identify themselves. They seized the 54-year-old Vasquez Perdomo, handcuffed him, chained his feet, waist and hands, and hauled him away. No one showed him a warrant or told him why they were arresting him, he later wrote in a declaration . “It felt like a kidnapping,” he wrote. The agents drove Vasquez Perdomo and his coworkers to B-18, an immigration processing site in the basement of a federal building in downtown Los Angeles. Some lawyers had dubbed the facility a “black hole,” because detainees could be hard to locate or reach there. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement did not respond to requests for comment for this story. Attorneys often can’t figure out where ICE is detaining people—and can’t see the evidence against them.
